title: Return to sport decisions after an acute lateral ankle sprain injury: introducing the PAASS framework—an international multidisciplinary consensus
claims: A three-round Delphi survey of 155 globally diverse health professionals reached consensus (>70% agreement) on 16 assessment items to support the return-to-sport decision after an acute lateral ankle sprain.
The 16 items map to five PAASS domains: Pain, Ankle impairments, Athlete perception, Sensorimotor control, and Sport/functional performance, with 98% panellist agreement on the mapping.
Sport/functional performance items include hopping (87% agreement), jumping (84%), agility (87%), sport-specific activities (98%), and ability to complete a full training session (87%).
Pain items retained are severity during sport participation (93%) and over the last 24 hours (81%); pain over the last week and pain on palpation were excluded.
Athlete perception items are perceived reassurance/confidence (81%), perceived stability (74%), and psychological readiness (74%).
Structural integrity of the ligaments on imaging was excluded from the RTS decision (89% agreement), as was ligamentous laxity (81%).
Return to sport was defined as being sanctioned for unrestricted training and cleared or available for match play or competition selection.
